purpose: Native-speaker validation set. Strings here reach farmers verbatim once validated and added to agbe/translate/messages.py. Unreviewed rows are excluded from any claim.
instructions_for_reviewer: Fill the last column of the exported CSV: OK approves, anything else replaces. Draft cells are EMPTY on purpose - machine drafts were measured deleting prohibition clauses in this language pair and are not offered. Compose from the English.

safety_messages.purpose: Refusal - shown when the corpus cannot answer
safety_messages.english: I do not have local guidance on that in my documents, so I cannot give you a reliable answer. Please ask your local extension officer.

safety_messages.purpose: Warning - a cited pesticide is hazardous/banned
safety_messages.english: Some sources mention pesticides that are banned or severely restricted in many countries. Do not use them. Ask your local extension officer which products are currently registered for your crop.

safety_messages.purpose: A dosage in the answer is not in the sources
safety_messages.english: This answer contained application rates that are not stated in the source documents, so they have been removed. Never guess a dose - ask an extension officer or read the product label.

safety_messages.purpose: Chemical advice comes only from old documents
safety_messages.english: Chemical control guidance here comes from older documents. Pesticide registrations change; confirm with an extension officer before applying anything.

safety_messages.purpose: Refusal to state any pesticide/drug dose
safety_messages.english: I cannot tell you how much to use. The correct amount depends on the specific product and what is registered for your crop or animal. Read the product label, or ask your extension officer.

IMPORTANT: after treating an animal with medicine, there is a withdrawal period before its milk or meat is safe for people to consume. Ask a veterinary officer how long to wait before selling or drinking the milk, or slaughtering the animal.

safety_messages.purpose: Redirect to a clinic - human health symptom
safety_messages.english: If you feel unwell after handling farm chemicals, stop work, wash thoroughly, and go to a clinic or hospital now. Take the product container with you so they know what you were exposed to.

safety_messages.purpose: Polite refusal for crops we do not cover
safety_messages.english: I do not cover that crop. My documents are about cassava, maize, yam, tomato, rice, cowpea, groundnut, pepper and okra, and about livestock. Please ask your extension officer.

advisory_samples.english: Your cassava has mosaic disease. The leaves become yellow and twisted, and the plant stays small.
Remove the infected plants and destroy them away from your farm.
Only take stem cuttings from healthy plants that show no symptoms.
Whiteflies carry the virus from one plant to another.
These signs suggest Newcastle disease. Separate the sick birds immediately and dispose of dead birds properly.
Store the maize and sell it later, but dry it well first so weevils do not spoil it.
Wait until the rains are steady before you plant, not after the first shower.
Check your field every week and look under the leaves for insects.
